Ultrarapid drug metabolism: PCR-based detection of CYP2D6 gene duplication. The enzyme debrisoquine 4-hydroxylase (CYP2D6), which metabolizes many widely used drugs, is highly polymorphic. The activity of the enzyme ranges between subjects from ultrafast to a complete absence. Therefore, metabolic capacity varies, producing intersubject differences in therapeutic efficacy and side effects at standard recommended doses. Up to 7% of Caucasians may demonstrate ultrarapid drug metabolism (UM) because of inherited alleles with multiplicate functional CYP2D6 genes, causing an increased amount of enzyme to be expressed.
